root_cause.text: The microchip-core-qspi driver's `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` incorrectly handled read-only dual/quad SPI transfers by using the write-read path and transmitting dummy TX data, even though the QSPI core must generate read clocks itself and does not have a separate MOSI-style output for such operations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `dual_quad` detection and changes the `t->rx_buf` path from always calling `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi)` to calling `mchp_coreqspi_read_op(qspi)` for dual/quad transfers; the commit/CVE text explicitly says that "transmitting garbage data just bricks the transfer" and that "the core will deal with reads by creating clock cycles itself."

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the read-only operation for dual/quad SPI receive transfers so multi-bit reads are handled correctly instead of going through the normal write-read path.
intent_record.what: The function `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` adds a new local boolean `dual_quad` initialized to `false`, sets it to `true` when either `t->tx_nbits` or `t->rx_nbits` indicates `SPI_NBITS_DUAL` or `SPI_NBITS_QUAD`, and changes the receive-side branching so that transfers with `rx_buf` use `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi)` only when `dual_quad` is false, while dual/quad receive transfers instead initialize `qspi->rxbuf` and `qspi->rx_len` and call `mchp_coreqspi_read_op(qspi)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes SPI transfers that use dual- or quad-bit modes follow a dedicated read path instead of the combined write-read path when receiving data. This avoids handling dual/quad RX transfers as normal full-duplex operations and enables the controller to perform reads correctly for multi-bit bus modes.

grouping_result.intent: Use the read-only operation for dual/quad SPI receive transfers so multi-bit reads are handled correctly instead of going through the normal write-read path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it switches dual/quad SPI receive transfers from the incorrect write-read path to the proper read-only operation, preventing transmission of dummy TX data and letting the QSPI core generate read clocks correctly.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct buggy operation selection for transfers with an rx buffer. It routes read-only dual/quad receive transfers through the write-read path, causing dummy TX data to be transmitted instead of using the hardware's read-only clock-generation path.
This condition only distinguishes transfers by presence of an rx buffer, so any transfer with rx_buf set—including read-only dual/quad reads—is forced into the else branch and mishandled.

For read-only receive transfers, assigning tx_len to the transfer length contributes to treating the operation as if transmit data should be sent, matching the root cause of dummy TX bytes being clocked out.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement selects the write-read path for transfers in the rx-buffer case, which is the root cause: read-only dual/quad receive operations were incorrectly executed as write-read transfers, causing dummy TX data to be transmitted instead of using the QSPI core's read-only clock-generation path.

This condition partitions handling solely on whether an rx buffer exists, so read-only dual/quad receive transfers fall into the non-write-only branch and are subsequently routed to the wrong operation type.

For read-only receive transfers, this sets a transmit length equal to the receive length, reinforcing the incorrect assumption that bytes should be transmitted during the operation and contributing to the dummy-TX behavior.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers

The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full newly added regular-transfer path, especially `mchp_coreqspi_prepare_message()` and `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()`, which determine how read/write transfers are executed.

The vulnerable construct is present in `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()`. The code does:
- `if (!t->rx_buf) { mchp_coreqspi_write_op(qspi); } else { ... mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi); }`
This means every transfer with an RX buffer, including read-only transfers (`rx_buf != NULL` and `tx_buf == NULL`), is routed through `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`.

Inside `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`, the function explicitly transmits data while receiving:
- `qspi->rx_len = qspi->tx_len;`
- `data = qspi->txbuf ? *((u32 *)qspi->txbuf) : 0xaa;`
- `writel_relaxed(data, qspi->regs + REG_X4_TX_DATA);`
and later for tail bytes:
- `data = qspi->txbuf ? *qspi->txbuf : 0xaa;`
- `writel_relaxed(data, qspi->regs + REG_TX_DATA);`
So when `tx_buf` is absent, dummy TX bytes `0xaa` are sent during RX transfers.

That matches the root cause: read-only dual/quad transfers are incorrectly handled by the write-read path and dummy TX data is transmitted instead of using a dedicated read-clock generation behavior.

The fix is not present. There is no special-case handling in `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` for read-only dual/quad RX transfers, no separate receive-only path, and no condition preventing `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` from being used when `tx_buf` is NULL. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
